overview: The Medford Charter Study Committee met to review public participation rules, its draft work plan, and a public survey. The committee voted to continue focusing on a mayor-led executive branch rather than a city manager system unless public input directs otherwise.

items.title: New Member Status and Meeting Minutes
items.summary: The committee received a brief update on member recruitment and approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Public Participation Procedures
items.summary: The committee discussed allowing public comment after individual agenda items rather than solely at the end, but tabled the motion following a tie vote.

items.title: Draft Work Plan and Process
items.summary: Members discussed a proposed timeline and drafting process for the charter, including subcommittees and the logistics of ballot questions.

items.title: Public Survey Review
items.summary: The committee reviewed and revised the draft public survey, agreeing to include recall provisions and to consult the Health Department on demographic questions.

items.title: Executive Branch Deliberations
items.summary: The committee voted to table further consideration of a city manager form of government and continue focusing on a mayor-led system unless compelled by public feedback.

items.title: Official Interviews Progress
items.summary: Members shared scheduling updates for upcoming interviews with current and former city officials and department heads.

items.title: Focus Groups and Input Tracking Sheet
items.summary: The committee discussed fall focus group facilitator training with the Board of Health and reviewed a tracking spreadsheet for organizing public input.

items.title: Community Outreach Events
items.summary: Members discussed outreach plans for Wright's Pond and the Farmers Market, promotional signage, and scheduling an October public hearing at City Hall.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A resident provided feedback on survey methodology, committee efficiency, and the trade-offs of mayor and city manager forms of government.
